source_snapshot.procedure: Load BIOS defaults, save/reboot and compare this page with SPEC; then change `all/random` settings on the CRB Board page to non-default values, save/reboot and verify persistence.
source_snapshot.criteria: Defaults match SPEC, no error logs, normal reboot without hang/crash, and the non-default settings persist.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek recognizes manual BIOS navigation but describes a non-default-then-default-restore flow, reversing this source row's default-first then non-default-persistence sequence.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify the exact AMD-platform Advanced CRB Board defaults after Load Default, then verify that approved non-default CRB Board values persist across a subsequent save/reboot without platform regression.
original_test_intent.target: The owner-defined fields on the Advanced CRB Board BIOS page for the exact AMD board and firmware revision, including only the platform effects actually associated with those named fields.
original_test_intent.scope: First load defaults and compare the relevant CRB Board fields with SPEC; second, change the required fields to approved non-default values and prove persistence after reboot. The source's `all/random` phrase does not establish whether all fields or a sampled subset is required.
original_test_intent.operation: Archive the current deployed BIOS and platform inventory, perform the authorized Load Default/save/reboot and compare named CRB Board fields, apply a signed non-default field/value matrix manually, save/reboot and verify persistence, correlate only relevant board/topology/health effects, then place the SUT in the owner-approved final configuration.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One Load Default/save/reboot/default comparison followed by one non-default/save/reboot/persistence comparison. The 20-minute machine and 5-minute attended values are estimates.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Named CRB Board defaults exactly match the platform specification; every required non-default value persists after the second reboot; both reboots complete without hang/crash or unexplained error; all field-dependent board, boot, management and device behavior remains as specified.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Exact AMD board/BIOS identity, deployed baseline/configuration backup, engineer-approved all-versus-sample decision, field/default/non-default/dependency matrix, BIOS captures before and after each phase, reboot and health logs, field-specific inventory/topology checks, and approved final-state proof.
ambiguities: `all/random` leaves field coverage undefined and cannot support repeatable completion.
No CRB Board field names, allowed values, defaults or field-specific dependencies are provided.
Load Default may affect settings outside this page, while the source only asks to compare this function.
The source ends with non-default values and does not state whether that state or the prior deployed recipe is the required final state.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly treats the case as hybrid, restores default-first ordering, rejects random mutation, adds field-specific approval, read-only board/topology evidence and recovery. It implicitly replaces the unresolved all/random scope with a bounded set and lists broad possible platform effects without requiring each evidence check to be tied to the actual changed field.

applicable_history.decision: The historical record classifies the BIOS action as operator-only but does not preserve the source phase ordering or define the CRB field set.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain the hybrid classification: the operator must change BIOS values, while inventory and health comparisons can be automated. The AMD/platform owner must resolve field coverage, actual dependencies, global-default impact and final state before execution.

available_now: The source defines two ordered phases: defaults first, then non-default persistence.
Read-only board/BIOS/boot/device/management baselines and a supported configuration backup can be collected before mutation.
V2 already supplies recovery and hybrid manual-plus-automated boundaries.
missing_inputs: Exact CRB Board field list and an engineer decision on full versus sampled coverage
Per-field SPEC default, safe non-default value, dependency and expected observable effect for the exact AMD board/BIOS revision
Documented Load Default scope and collateral changes, plus current/deployed configuration backup
Owner-approved final state after the source's non-default-ending sequence, reboot/cold-boot requirement, maintenance window and recovery procedure
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The AMD platform/BIOS owner supplies field semantics, values, dependencies, reset requirements and final state; the system owner approves global defaults/reboots; the lab owner provides console, BMC/OOB, stable power, configuration recovery and an operator.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Capture exact board/BIOS/AGESA identifiers where exposed, current CRB page values, supported BIOS configuration backup/export, FRU/SMBIOS, boot and BMC/OOB health without clearing logs
Inventory only the CPU/memory/PCIe/device/topology areas plausibly affected by the candidate named fields, marking field-to-evidence mapping unresolved until vendor input arrives
prohibited_until_closed: Do not invoke Load Default, choose fields randomly, apply guessed AMD/CRB values, save/reboot or cold-boot before the field/dependency/final-state matrix is signed
Do not assume every CRB field affects memory/PCIe/power, accept generic inventory as proof, erase baseline logs or leave the SUT in an unspecified non-default state
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner-approved run card preserves default-first ordering, names every field/default/non-default/dependency, resolves all versus sample, documents global default effects and reboot type, validates backup/OOB recovery, and states the exact final configuration.

revision_candidate.test_name: AMD Advanced CRB Board Defaults and Persistence
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify platform-specified CRB Board defaults after Load Default, then verify approved non-default CRB values persist through save/reboot with no field-related platform regression.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact AMD server board, BIOS/AGESA build and hardware recipe in a maintenance environment with platform documentation, a recoverable BIOS baseline, console, BMC/OOB access and stable power.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the owner-named Advanced CRB Board fields and their documented dependencies. The owner must declare complete or sampled coverage; unrelated memory/PCIe/power checks are not added without a field dependency.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Board/BIOS/AGESA identity; signed coverage decision; per-field default/non-default/dependency matrix; Load Default collateral map; backup; reboot/cold-boot rule; final-state decision; approvals, console/operator, OOB recovery and evidence plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Archive the deployed baseline; manually load defaults, save/reboot and compare each named field with SPEC; manually apply only signed non-default values, save and perform the specified reboot type; verify persistence and each field-linked system effect; restore/retain exactly the owner-approved final configuration and verify health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Field semantics and values documented; correct AMD platform/build selected; deployed configuration recoverable; global default impact and final state approved; field-specific expected evidence defined; boot window, operator, OOB/recovery and power ready; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identity and signed matrix; recoverable baseline; default-phase captures and comparisons; non-default and post-reboot captures; exact reboot timeline; per-field linked inventory/health/log evidence; collateral-default diff; final configuration and normal boot/BMC/OS proof.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact AMD platform/vendor BIOS specification for the named CRB Board fields and firmware revision, plus the approved hardware recipe and final configuration record.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never use random or guessed values, generalize another AMD platform's defaults, mutate unnamed fields, invoke global defaults without collateral approval, continue after boot/topology/management loss, clear logs or release an unspecified final configuration.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform/BIOS and system owners approve every field/value, global default operation, reboot type and final state. A human operator performs the pre-OS changes; owners judge field-specific exceptions.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: BIOS navigation, Load Default, field editing and visual value readback are manual. Automated support is limited to approved inventory, topology, health, log and configuration comparisons around those phases.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On failed boot/training, device loss, management outage or unexpected setting effect, stop changes, preserve console/state evidence, use the documented BMC/OOB/vendor recovery and captured configuration, then verify the entire approved hardware and BIOS recipe before retry.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved coverage/field semantics/defaults/dependencies/final state; missing backup/approval/OOB; unexpected collateral default; value rejection or failed persistence; incorrect reboot behavior; boot/training/device/management/health regression; or inability to restore the approved configuration.

identified_defects: DeepSeek reverses the source sequence and would test a different end state.
The source's `all/random` instruction is irreproducible and unsafe without a platform field matrix.
V2 does not explicitly bind its broad topology/health checks to actual field dependencies and silently chooses a bounded coverage model.
reason_for_change: Preserve the source's default-first/non-default-last intent, require the engineer to resolve its field-coverage ambiguity, and prevent generic AMD risk assumptions from replacing field-specific platform evidence.
removed_ambiguities: Fixes the phase order relative to DeepSeek's reversed description.
Separates known manual BIOS actions from automatable field-specific health evidence.
Makes final non-default-versus-deployed state an explicit owner decision.
resolved_blockers: Manual BIOS mutation does not make the whole case MANUAL ONLY because approved read-only comparisons can be automated; missing vendor data remains readiness input.
remaining_blockers: No mutation until field coverage, exact values/dependencies, global default effect, reboot type, recovery and final state are approved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains V2's useful hybrid model and recovery safeguards but enforces the source's actual phase order, exposes rather than silently resolves all/random coverage, and requires each automated topology/health check to trace to a named CRB field.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The isolated validator retained default-first then approved non-default Advanced CRB phases, required reboot ordering, collateral review and owner-approved final state.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: This source loads and verifies AMD CRB defaults first, then ends by proving approved non-default settings persist after a second reboot.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 restores phase order and hybrid evidence but silently bounds all/random and does not require field-to-health-evidence traceability.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Require named AMD CRB fields, exact values/dependencies, recoverable global-default baseline and owner-defined final state before either BIOS mutation.
